findings.body: The SMS scheduler's deleteMany query deletes that non-SMS reminder even if its scheduled date has not passed, causing an unrelated email or WhatsApp notification to be lost.
findings.failure_mode: The cleanup operation applies an SMS-specific retry policy to every WorkflowReminder method.
findings.impact: The SMS scheduler's deleteMany query deletes that non-SMS reminder even if its scheduled date has not passed, causing an unrelated email or WhatsApp notification to be lost.
findings.root_cause: The new retryCount deletion predicate is an OR branch without a WorkflowMethods.SMS constraint.
findings.suggested_fix: Add method: WorkflowMethods.SMS to the retryCount OR branch (or wrap both alternatives in an SMS method constraint).
findings.title: Scope the retry cleanup to SMS reminders
findings.trigger: An EMAIL or WHATSAPP WorkflowReminder has retryCount greater than 1, such as a backfilled or otherwise populated reminder row, when the SMS scheduler endpoint runs.
findings.verifier_reason: Patch lines R38-R42 add an OR branch with only `retryCount: { gt: 1 }` and no `method: WorkflowMethods.SMS` constraint. This deleteMany will delete any WorkflowReminder (EMAIL, WHATSAPP, etc.) with retryCount > 1, regardless of method. The cited line 39 exists verbatim, the cause is introduced by the patch, the trigger is realistic (any non-SMS reminder with retryCount > 1), and the impact (unintended deletion) follows directly.

pr.body:
## What does this PR do?

Right now when SMS fails to send because of whatever reason (e.g. invalid phone number), we are trying to keep scheduling it in our corn job until the date is reached. This PR introduces a retry count, after scheduling failed twice we delete the workflow reminder.
pr.title: fix: add retryCount to workflowReminder

raw_findings.body: The SMS scheduler's deleteMany query deletes that non-SMS reminder even if its scheduled date has not passed, causing an unrelated email or WhatsApp notification to be lost.
raw_findings.failure_mode: The cleanup operation applies an SMS-specific retry policy to every WorkflowReminder method.
raw_findings.impact: The SMS scheduler's deleteMany query deletes that non-SMS reminder even if its scheduled date has not passed, causing an unrelated email or WhatsApp notification to be lost.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new retryCount deletion predicate is an OR branch without a WorkflowMethods.SMS constraint.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add method: WorkflowMethods.SMS to the retryCount OR branch (or wrap both alternatives in an SMS method constraint).
raw_findings.title: Scope the retry cleanup to SMS reminders
raw_findings.trigger: An EMAIL or WHATSAPP WorkflowReminder has retryCount greater than 1, such as a backfilled or otherwise populated reminder row, when the SMS scheduler endpoint runs.

raw_findings.body: Both updates write the same next value instead of recording both failures, so a reminder that has already failed twice remains eligible for another scheduling attempt rather than being cleaned up.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Concurrent scheduler executions lose retry attempts and violate the two-failure retry limit.
raw_findings.impact: Both updates write the same next value instead of recording both failures, so a reminder that has already failed twice remains eligible for another scheduling attempt rather than being cleaned up.
raw_findings.root_cause: The retry count is computed from a stale value read before the update rather than incremented atomically in the database.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Use Prisma's atomic field operation, retryCount: { increment: 1 }, for this update.
raw_findings.title: Atomically increment retries after a falsy scheduling result
raw_findings.trigger: Two overlapping authorized cron invocations read the same unscheduled reminder with the same retryCount and twilio.scheduleSMS returns no scheduled message in both invocations.

raw_findings.body: The catch handlers can overwrite each other's retry count, causing the reminder to survive past two failed attempts and be submitted again.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Concurrent failures are undercounted, so retry cleanup is delayed and extra scheduling attempts occur.
raw_findings.impact: The catch handlers can overwrite each other's retry count, causing the reminder to survive past two failed attempts and be submitted again.
raw_findings.root_cause: The exception retry update uses the stale retryCount selected at the start of each concurrent invocation.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Replace the read-modify-write assignment with retryCount: { increment: 1 } in the exception path as well.
raw_findings.title: Atomically increment retries after scheduling exceptions
raw_findings.trigger: Two overlapping cron invocations attempt the same reminder and both scheduling paths throw, for example because Twilio rejects an invalid number.

raw_findings.body: The retry update throws because the row no longer exists, escapes the catch block, and terminates the handler before later reminders in the batch are processed.
raw_findings.failure_mode: A normal concurrent deletion converts one reminder failure into a failed cron request and skips subsequent reminders.
raw_findings.impact: The retry update throws because the row no longer exists, escapes the catch block, and terminates the handler before later reminders in the batch are processed.
raw_findings.root_cause: An awaited database update was added inside the catch block without handling failures from that update itself.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Handle errors from the retry update separately and ignore a missing-record error (or use an updateMany keyed by id), then continue processing the remaining reminders.
raw_findings.title: Do not let a retry-update failure abort the whole reminder batch
raw_findings.trigger: A reminder is selected by this cron run and then deleted by a concurrent booking cancellation before scheduling fails or before the successful-scheduling update completes.

finding.trigger: Two overlapping authorized cron invocations read the same unscheduled reminder with the same retryCount and twilio.scheduleSMS returns no scheduled message in both invocations.
finding.verifier_reason: Line 184 `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1` exists verbatim. The patch introduces this read-modify-write pattern. Concurrent cron invocations reading the same reminder before either updates could both compute the same incremented value, causing lost updates. However, the trigger requires overlapping cron executions processing the same reminder, which may be unlikely depending on deployment. The race is theoretically possible but requires specific timing.
